provenance: 150 queries generated in this Phase 2 session. 105 queries (classes A-G) were built from 24 deterministic templates parameterized over a curated, live-API-verified entity list (8 diseases via NLM MeSH lookup, 8 genes/targets via HGNC rest.genenames.org, 8 compounds via ChEMBL's own REST API - all verified during this session, IDs recorded in nlu/normalization.py) - gold intent/entities/constraints/required_sources are the template's own substitution parameters, not an LLM opinion. 30 queries (classes H, I) were hand-authored directly by the agent acting as the session's human reviewer (per explicit task instruction, since no other human reviewer was available), with labels assigned by direct reading of each query's text, not by asking an LLM for the correct label. No query in this benchmark had its gold label produced by asking an LLM 'what is the correct label' and accepting the answer - this is a hard requirement per BENCHMARK_PLAN.md 3. v1.1.0 migration (Phase 2 closure): 15 examples' intent_class relabeled from H_insufficient_evidence to their query-time surface class by the agent re-reading each query's text (same methodology as original authoring - no LLM was asked for the correct label); 1 example's required_sources corrected (nlu_v1_0121) and 1 example's constraints corrected to include a previously-missing status constraint (nlu_v1_0126, 'completed Phase 4 trials' implies both a phase AND a status constraint). Full diff in artifacts/v2/nlu_closure_benchmark_migration.json.
known_limitations: Single-annotator (the agent, acting as reviewer) - no second independent human annotator or adjudication pass was available in this session; BENCHMARK_PLAN.md calls for >=1 reviewer minimum, which is met, but inter-annotator agreement could not be computed.

Template-generated examples (105/150) are lexically homogeneous within a template family - real user queries will have more surface-form variety than 24 fixed templates capture; this is a known ceiling-effect risk on extraction metrics, flagged for a future benchmark revision.

Entity normalization gold labels are limited to the 24 curated entities (8 disease/8 gene/8 compound) in nlu/normalization.py's tables - normalization accuracy on this benchmark does not generalize to entities outside that table.
Class boundary D vs E and B vs G were assigned using the fixed rule in nlu/taxonomy.py (DI_VS_E_RULE) applied by the agent during template design, not validated by a second annotator.
n=15-23 per class is enough for a first F1 estimate per BENCHMARK_PLAN.md's own stated expectation, not for a tight confidence interval - reported explicitly per class, not just in aggregate.

v1.1.0 (Phase 2 CLOSURE item 5): H_insufficient_evidence removed as a query-time gold label. PRODUCT_CONTRACT.md defines H as a post-retrieval evidence-sufficiency outcome ('any of the above where sources return nothing usable'), not a property of query text; the NLU stage runs before any tool call and structurally cannot determine it (confirmed: 0/15 v1.0.0 H examples were ever predicted as H by either candidate on either split). The 15 examples gold-labeled H in v1.0.0 were relabeled to the query-time class a text-only reader would assign from their surface form (their original entities/query text are unchanged; two examples also had a gold required_sources/constraints correction - see artifacts/v2/nlu_closure_benchmark_migration.json for the full per-example diff and justification). This is a labeling-layer correction, not new query material, and does not add or remove any example from either split (still 45/105/150).

Benchmark reaudit (Phase 2 closure item 16): gold entity types actually used across all 150 examples are ONLY 'disease', 'target', and 'compound' - 'gene', 'protein', and 'intervention' (all declared in nlu/schemas.py::EntityType) have ZERO gold examples in this benchmark. Any entity-typing or normalization quality claim for gene/protein/intervention specifically is therefore unmeasured by this benchmark, not just unmeasured-and-good - this is a genuine coverage gap, not something either NLU candidate can be faulted for. Constraint values for trial_phases/trial_statuses ARE already consistently canonical (PHASE1-4, RECRUITING/COMPLETED/ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING/... - verified by direct inspection, no non-canonical forms found), so nlu/normalization.py's canonicalize_trial_phase/canonicalize_trial_status (added this closure pass) are validated against real-world free-text LLM output, not against the benchmark's own (already-canonical) gold values. Extending the benchmark with gene/protein/intervention examples is out of this closure pass's bounded scope (would be new benchmark material, not a labeling correction) and is left as an open item for a future benchmark revision.
